title: Module 5: Types, Grammar, Coercion & Equality (All Chapters)
description: Comprehensive module-level assessment covering all chapters of Module 5: Types, Grammar, Coercion & Equality.

cards.concept: Primitive Types & Reference Types: Abstract Equality vs Strict Equality Algorithm
cards.question: What is the key difference between strict equality (`===`) and abstract equality (`==`) according to ECMA-262?

options.text: `===` coerces strings to numbers, whereas `==` compares raw pointers.
`===` returns false immediately if operand types differ; `==` applies recursive implicit coercion rules before comparing.
`==` throws a TypeError if types do not match.

cards.explanation: The strict equality operator (===) checks Type(x) === Type(y) first without coercion. Abstract equality (==) coerces booleans and strings to numbers, and objects to primitives via ToPrimitive.
cards.codeSnippet:
console.log(0 == ''); // true ('' coerced to 0)
console.log(0 === ''); // false (number !== string)
console.log(null == undefined); // true
console.log(null === undefined); // false
cards.pitfall: Relying on abstract equality with truthy/falsy checks causes subtle bugs with 0, '', false, and empty arrays [].
cards.citation: ECMAScript 2024 Specification §7.2.14 / You Don't Know JS: Types & Grammar

cards.concept: Primitive Types & Reference Types: Symbol.toPrimitive & Object Coercion
cards.question: When an object is coerced to a primitive (e.g. in arithmetic or template literals), which method has top priority in ECMAScript?
cards.explanation: The ECMAScript ToPrimitive abstract operation checks for [Symbol.toPrimitive] first. If present, it calls it with hint ('number', 'string', or 'default'). If absent, it falls back to valueOf() and toString().
cards.pitfall: Returning an object from [Symbol.toPrimitive] throws a TypeError; it must return a primitive value.
cards.citation: ECMAScript 2024 Specification §7.1.1 / MDN Web Docs: Symbol.toPrimitive
